turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): I'll grab a quick set of vitals before he sits down. Blood pressure is 118 over 74, pulse 96, oxygen 98 percent on room air.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Is 96 too fast? I've been anxious in the waiting room and my hands are sweaty.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Could just be nerves. Respirations were 16. He'll be right in.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hey, sorry, this thing is still loading. What are we seeing you for?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm exhausted, I get breathless, and my periods are really heavy. I almost cancelled because I felt silly, but I can't keep doing this.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Exhausted and breathless. Hold on, the screen jumped. Say the period part again?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Heavy periods. They've been like this for ten months... no, actually a full year, since last spring around my birthday.
[SEG0008] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Oh honey, it's been longer than a year. A year and a half, at least. I remember you complaining the Christmas before last.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Mom, that was cramps, not this. The heavy bleeding started about a year ago. I know my own body.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay, I'll put roughly a year to a year and a half, since you two aren't landing on the same number. How many pads, and any clots?

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't count pads exactly. Way more than I used to, like I ruin them, and there are clots, kind of big. Bigger than a grape, or maybe that's dramatic, and not every day.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say the clot size once more. I was clicking the wrong tab.

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Clots, sometimes around grape size, I think. The bleeding goes seven or eight days... well, actually it's more like nine or ten days now. Not between periods, though, just the period.
[SEG0014] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She also gets dizzy when she stands up. I've seen her grab the kitchen counter, and the stairs wipe her out so she stops halfway.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I do not get dizzy, and I have not grabbed the counter. I do get short of breath on the stairs and if I'm hauling laundry, but that's it. Mom, please.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): You two disagree on the dizziness, so I'll leave that unsettled. When did the shortness of breath start? Say it again, I only half heard.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): I can't really date it. Um, a few months? It crept up and I don't know.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright, onset unclear. Is the tiredness constant?

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Pretty much all day. I sleep and I'm still wiped out, and my hair's coming out in the shower. I almost said handfuls, but it's not handfuls, just more than normal for a couple of months. Is hair loss a sign of something terrible?
[SEG0020] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The hair has been at least six months. I see it on the bathroom floor all the time.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): It is not six months. Two months, three tops. Why are you making it sound worse?
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hair loss, call it somewhere between two and six months. I'm not refereeing that. How old are you, and any chance of pregnancy? The chart age didn't load.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm 36, and I really don't think I'm pregnant since my husband had a vasectomy. But could this be cancer? I was up at 2 a.m. reading, so would you tell me straight?
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cancer's not the first thing I'm thinking, and I won't promise anything without tests. Any chest pain?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain. If you won't promise, does that mean it might be? I'm sorry, I know I ask a lot.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): It means I need data, not that I'm hiding a bad answer. Any fainting?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I haven't fainted. What are you actually going to test, and does the needle hurt? I hate needles.
[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thyroid runs in the family. I have hypothyroidism, and her aunt Carol had thyroid trouble too. That can make you tired and lose hair, right?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Nobody's ever told me I have a thyroid problem. So are you checking that, and if it's low do I take a pill forever? Mom, you're scaring me.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): TSH is going on the order. Wrong set, hang on. You take iron, right? Say it again, I was reading a popup.

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, ferrous gluconate... no, ferrous sulfate, 325 milligrams. They said once a day, but I only take it sometimes, when I remember. Can iron wreck your stomach? Mine's been a little off... wait, no, my stomach is fine, forget that.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): 325 of ferrous sulfate, got it. What was it prescribed for?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Low iron, they said at an urgent care. That was a while ago, and I couldn't tell you the month. I don't remember the number they quoted either.
[SEG0034] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And she skips it more than she takes it. I put the bottle on the counter and it just sits there.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): So you're not taking it the way it was prescribed. Try for that 325 every day, with a little food, not with your coffee. I'm not adding a second iron.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Not with coffee, okay. What about tea in the afternoon? And sometimes my heart feels fast when I'm anxious, so is that the anemia or just me spiraling?

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tea later is fine, just not right with the pill. The heart racing I'm not chasing separately today, the blood count will help. Quick look, your lower lids are pale, lungs are clear, and there's no swelling in the ankles that I can see.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Pale sounds really bad. Are you saying I have anemia, and do I need a transfusion? My friend got one and she said it was awful, I don't want that.

[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): No transfusion talk. My working thought is this may be iron deficiency from the heavy periods, but that's provisional until labs are back. I also can't rule out a thyroid issue with your family history.

[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): So what labs exactly, and do I need a scan? I read about fibroids and I'm scared that means a hysterectomy, and I still want kids. He was going to reverse the vasectomy... wait, no, he hasn't, I'm just talking too much.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm ordering a CBC, a ferritin, and a TSH today. If the bloodwork doesn't explain the bleeding, we might do a pelvic ultrasound. Nobody is booking surgery.
[SEG0042] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Can she get the blood drawn here before we go? She's cancelled labs twice already.
[SEG0043] person_1 (NURSE): If the orders are in, I can draw them right after this. Just a couple of tubes, a quick pinch.

[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Is the ultrasound today too, because I don't want to wait if something's growing? Do I have to fast? I already had coffee and a muffin, and if follow-up is two weeks, what if I can't function at work before then?

[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): No fasting. The ultrasound is not today, and we might only order it if the labs don't explain the bleeding. Come back in two weeks for the results, even if you feel better.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks is a long time when I'm this tired. If I can't catch my breath, do I go to the ER? I work reception and I'm on my feet, so can I still go in?

[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): If you get severely short of breath, chest pain, or you pass out, go to the ER. Otherwise work as you're able and sit when you need to. I have to finish this note, the system keeps spinning.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Thanks. Mom, please don't call Aunt Carol about this, I'm embarrassed enough.
[SEG0049] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I won't. Let's go get that blood drawn before you change your mind.

spec.situation: Tired, breathless woman with heavy periods for a year; counts pads and clots in vague terms; takes iron 'sometimes'; hair loss; relative mentions thyroid in the family. Blood tests, maybe pelvic scan.
features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Symptom and triggers supported, but certainty is wrong; patient states it, not uncertain.
bad.text: shortness of breath (category=respiratory, status=present, onset=unclear, temporality=current, aggravating_factors=climbing stairs and carrying laundry, reported_by=patient, certainty=uncertain)

omissions.text: Pregnancy considered unlikely because husband had a vasectomy.
Heavy menstrual bleeding includes clots sometimes around grape size.
Shortness of breath has been present for a few months, though onset is imprecise/crept up.
Tiredness persists despite sleep ('I sleep and I'm still wiped out').
Prior history of low iron diagnosed at urgent care, timing unknown and prior value not remembered.
Blood draw could be done in clinic right after the visit if orders are in.
Follow-up instruction was to return in two weeks for results even if she feels better.
Doctor specifically advised not to add a second iron supplement.
